title: Mindspark after-school centers in Delhi: voucher lottery winners score 0.37 SD higher in math and 0.23 SD in Hindi after 4.5 months (AER 2019, J-PAL)
summary: Lottery evaluation of Educational Initiatives' Mindspark software plus small-group instruction among 619 Delhi public-school students: +0.37 SD math, +0.23 SD Hindi in 4.5 months.
account: Educational Initiatives (EI) ran three after-school Mindspark centers in Delhi serving low-income neighborhoods, where each 90-minute session combined 45 minutes of self-driven work on the Mindspark software, which the J-PAL summary says uses data to identify each student's learning level, deliver content at that level and adjust to progress, with 45 minutes of small-group instruction by a teaching assistant, six days a week. Muralidharan, Singh and Ganimian recruited 619 students from five public middle schools near the centers in September 2015; about half won a lottery for a voucher that waived fees until February 2016, when an endline test was taken. The American Economic Review paper (April 2019) reports that lottery winners scored 0.37 sigma higher in math and 0.23 sigma higher in Hindi over the 4.5-month period, with instrumental-variable estimates of 0.6 and 0.39 sigma for 90 days of attendance; the NBER version states that the intent-to-treat estimates reflect 58% average attendance. J-PAL gives a per-student monthly cost of about INR 1,000 against INR 1,500 in public schools. The date observed is the first day of the recruitment month (September 2015), used as a placeholder; the sources give months, not days.
purpose: Mindspark was built to personalize instruction to each student's measured level; the test-score gains are that purpose.
system: Mindspark computer-assisted learning software (personalized, adaptive) delivered in after-school Mindspark centers with small-group instructional support
deployer: Educational Initiatives' Mindspark centers (three centers in Delhi)

ratings.reason: General benefit without an individually attributable event: lottery winners gained 0.37 SD in math and 0.23 SD in Hindi over 4.5 months (AER abstract, J-PAL summary).
General benefit without an event: the deployer gained independent evidence for the center model at about INR 1,000 per student per month (J-PAL summary).

ai_role.statement: The software delivered half of each session and the other half was small-group instruction by teaching assistants, so the evaluated effect is of the combined program; the papers attribute the gains to precise targeting of instruction to student level.

produced_by: Software that continuously assessed each student and served content at the measured level rather than the grade level
Ninety-minute sessions six days a week split between software and small-group instruction
A voucher lottery among 619 students from five public middle schools near three centers, with endline testing in February 2016
must_hold: Students far below grade level, so targeted content has room to help (the papers report similar absolute gains but larger relative gains for weaker students)
Attendance at the centers (ITT estimates reflect 58% average attendance per the NBER version)

headline: Mindspark raises Delhi students' math scores by 0.37 SD
metric: +0.37 SD math, +0.23 SD Hindi in 4.5 months

comparator.against: lottery losers (comparison group) who did not receive the Mindspark voucher
comparator.before: the comparison group's gains over the same 4.5 months (less than half as large; near zero for weaker students)
comparator.after: 0.37 standard deviations higher in math and 0.23 standard deviations higher in Hindi for voucher winners
comparator.quote: Students offered a voucher scored 0.37 standard deviations higher in math, improving by over twice as much as students in the comparison group.

later.note: A 2025 NBER working paper reports an 18-month experiment of Mindspark adapted into Rajasthan government school schedules, in a sample over 20 times larger, with gains of 0.22 SD in math and 0.20 SD in Hindi, and scale-ups now reaching over 250,000 students.
later.quote: After 18 months, treated students scored 0.22σ higher in Mathematics and 0.20σ higher in Hindi, a 50–66% productivity increase over the control group. Learning gains were proportional to student time on the platform, providing a simple, low-cost metric for monitoring implementation quality in future scale-ups. The adaptation and its experimental validation have informed scale-ups now reaching over 250,000 students.
